Many applications that you create with [[T0]] are self-contained solutions to a specific business requirement. For example, you might create a [[T1]] application to track your customers, which can include not only database information about the customers, but tools for taking orders, invoicing, and so on. You can create all the features your application needs using the facilities already available in [[T2]], including its database engine, visual design tools, and reporting capabilities.

You can also use [[T3]] as part of a larger-scale application that involves two or more development tools. Using [[T4]] this way — referred to as "enterprise development" — allows you to take advantage of the unique capabilities of each product. Enterprise development can be as simple as maintaining a customer database in [[T5]] and creating a mail merge letter in Microsoft Word, or it can involve creating a complex application using client/server databases, Automation servers, electronic mail, and more.

[[T0]] is an ideal tool for creating enterprise-wide business solutions because it features:
 - Powerful, easy-to-use application development tools, including a Form Designer and wizards.
- A fast database engine.
- Excellent connectivity with other products, including both other Windows programs such as Microsoft Excel and Word, and client/server systems such as Microsoft [[T1]] Server.
- Integrated source control and other team development tools.

These features allow you to develop with [[T2]] in several roles in an enterprise-wide application. You can use [[T3]]:
 - As a front end for other applications. In this scenario, you work primarily with [[T4]]; for example, you create the user interface for the application in [[T5]]. You then access other applications that contain data needed for the application or that can provide services that enhance those already available in [[T6]]. You can also upsize your [[T7]] data or move it to another platform.
- As a data source for other applications. To do so, you would create the user interface for the application using another program, and then access [[T8]] data as needed.

The strategy you choose depends on what your application goals are and what programs you want to use.

[[T0]]

Specifies the name of an application or program that the [[T1]] Report System calls when a suitable [[T2]] command occurs.

The [[T0]] Report System invokes the application specified by this value when one of the following conditions occur:
 - You invoke the [[T1]] or [[T2]] command with an explicit [[T3]] <N> clause. The Report Engine passes the numeric value you use to the application named in _REPORTOUTPUT .
- You invoke a [[T4]] command after having used the command [[T5]] 90 . This setting indicates that you want to use object-assisted mode for all [[T6]] or [[T7]] commands. The Report Engine uses the other keywords on the output command (such as [[T8]] or [[T9]] ) to establish the appropriate numeric value for the equivalent [[T10]] <N> clause.

In both scenarios, the Report Engine also passes a variable to the application specified in _REPORTOUTPUT. The application stores a reference to an appropriate ReportListener object to this variable. In the subsequent report or label processing run, the Report Engine partners with this object to handle output rendering.

By default, _REPORTOUTPUT specifies the path and file name for the [[T11]] located in the main [[T12]] directory, as indicated by the [[T13]] function.

You can also specify a report output application using the File Locations tab in the Options dialog box. For more information, see File Locations Tab, Options Dialog Box.

When distributing applications, you may find it convenient to explicitly set _REPORTOUTPUT in the [[T0]] configuration file, [[T1]]. You can also set the _REPORTOUTPUT value to the name of a program built into your application. For more information, see Including Report Files for Distribution and Setting Configuration Options at Startup.

> **Note:** If you use a [[T2]] or [[T3]] command and include the [[T4]] <N> clause, or have previously used the command [[T5]] 90 , without a valid value in _REPORTOUTPUT , [[T6]] generates an error.

The application you specify with _REPORTOUTPUT must fulfill the following conditions:
 - It must accept at least two parameters. The Report Engine passes a numeric value, indicating the type of output required, as the first parameter. The Report Engine passes a variable, to hold a reference to an appropriate ReportListener, as the second parameter.
- It must store a [[T0]] value ( [[T1]] ) to the second parameter if it cannot understand the value in the first parameter, or does not have the ability to supply a reference to a ReportListener-derived object meeting the requirements of the first parameter.
- It must be able to provide ReportListener-derived object references for (at minimum) numeric types matching the native ListenerType values supported by [[T2]]. For more information, see ListenerType Property .
- If successful in obtaining a ReportListener object reference according to the numeric type requested by the ReportListener, it must store this reference to the second parameter. It must also store the numeric type supplied by the Report Engine or calling application to this object's OutputType property. For more information, see OutputType Property ([[T3]]) .
- It must be modal, because it must provide an appropriate reference back to the Report Engine. If it provides any user interface elements, for example allowing the user to select an appropriate ReportListener from a list, this interface should be modal as well.

The following additional conditions are not required for an application to function as _REPORTOUTPUT. However, fulfilling these conditions is highly recommended for any application in this capacity:
 - The application should maintain some type of ReportListener registry, to allow users to specify classes they prefer to use for various types of output.
- The application should bubble errors to the calling application in a manner that permits the caller to determine what action to take when the Report Output Application cannot meet its responsibilities.
